chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Dissatisfied with how Varsity Show used them
summary: Nazarro arranged it from New York; Bubbles thought they deserved better songs and scenes and did not ask for them.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: In instances like going off to Hollywood for "Varsity Show" was Nazarro with you, did he represent you then, did he come with you to the set or was that something that he just arranged from New York and you went off yourself?
He arranged it from New York.
Did you ever see the final --"Varsity Show" the final picture? The whole picture?
What was your feeling about it? Were you pleased with it? Were you pleased with yourself?
I wasn't satisfied because I thought he should have been with us, because I thought we should have had better than we did in the picture.
You think you should have done differently?

I think we should have had a different song to sing. We should have had different scenes to do. There were a lot of things that I thought could be done, that would get more out of us than we got out of us that would display our own talent than we got. We didn't get nothing, to my estimation.

That little thing we did on the piano that's all they wanted. But I thought it could have been much more than that. Buck could have played for dance for more than one person. I think so. But it didn't happen that way so I took it as it was.
Did you ask them to do additional things --
No, I didn't ask them nothing. I'm booked out there to do this picture and whatever they've got for me to do. So I don't ask nothing. I don't think it was my place to ask them.
On the other hand when you arrived they asked you -- they didn't have anything laid out for you. You had to sort of create your own --
That's right. That's right, exactly. Had to create our stuff ourselves, more or less to go in. But what can we do. Nothing.
